slides.heading: Ambiguous Measurements
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Recursion
slides.narration: Let's solve Ambiguous Measurements, a hard recursion problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Measuring cups each measure a [low, high] range.
Can repeated pours produce a volume within [low, high]?
Memoised search over remaining (low, high) targets.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Measuring cups each measure a low, high range. Can repeated pours produce a volume within low, high ? Memoised search over remaining (low, high) targets.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Try every cup recursively, shrinking the target range, and memoise the ranges already tried.
slides.narration: Try every cup recursively, shrinking the target range, and memoise the ranges already tried.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Memoised recursion on (low, high) → O(low · high · cups)
slides.narration: Trying every sequence of cups is exponential. Memoising on the remaining low and high bounds collapses repeats.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. If a cup fits inside the range, success
2. Otherwise subtract the cup from both bounds and recurse
slides.narration: Step by step. First, if a cup fits inside the range, success. Second, otherwise subtract the cup from both bounds and recurse. Third, memoise by range.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Can we always land in [2100, 2300]?
slides.narration: Each cup measures somewhere between its min and max. Can we guarantee a total between twenty-one hundred and twenty-three hundred?

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Subtract a cup's range and recurse
slides.narration: Using a cup shrinks the remaining range by its min and max. Recurse on the remaining range.

slides.heading: Worked example

lines: remaining [low, high] fits a cup: min ≥ low and max ≤ high → done

slides.caption: Memoise on (low, high)
slides.narration: We succeed when one cup's range fits inside the remaining range. The same remaining range repeats, so memoise on low and high.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Can memoises on low and high. A cup succeeds if its range fits; otherwise we recurse with the range reduced by the cup, clamped at zero.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of low times high times n. Space is O of low times high.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Clamp at zero, and skip cups that never make progress, to avoid infinite recursion.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Explain why low and high fully describe the state.

bullets: Try every cup recursively, shrinking the target range, and memoise the ranges already tried.
